The '''''Relentless''''' was an [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] which was best known as part of [[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] fleet during his campaign against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].

==History==
===Early service===
{{Quote|Our last patrol through Dalchon system netted us three pirate vessels, but ''Relentless'' sustained heavy damage to its hyperdrive engines. Of course, we captured a number of pirates. I was with Parlan when he interrogated one of the prisoners. What we heard still moves me. Commander Adar Tallon, hero of the Old Republic, is alive. And he's hiding on Tatooine.|Datapad entry of Rebel Agent Dana, serving undercover aboard the ''Relentless''|<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" />}}
The [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer]] ''Relentless'' was a [[Warship/Legends|warship]] in the [[Imperial Navy/Legends|Imperial Navy]].<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook">''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''</ref> [[Imperial Naval Academy/Legends|Naval Academy]] graduate [[Matt Turhaya]]'s first assignment was aboard the ''Relentless'', around three [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior to<ref name="Passages">{{JournalCite|7|Passages}}</ref> [[3 BBY/Legends|3 BBY]].<ref name="Reader's Companion">''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''</ref> The [[Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer's]] use of brute force to subdue local populations saw Turhaya become disgusted with the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and he deserted his post.<ref name="Passages" />

[[File:Relentlesstatooinemanhunt.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ''Relentless'']]
In [[1 BBY/Legends|1 BBY]], the ''Relentless'' and the ''[[Liberator (Imperial I-class)|Adjudicator]]'' were sent to [[Gerrard V]] to crush an [[Uprising on Gerrard V|uprising]] by a small [[Gerrard V Rebels|rebel navy]] that had circled the [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. The two Star [[Destroyer/Legends|Destroyers]] were under the command of [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Jion Trynn]]. After an Imperial strike team disabled Gerrard V's [[Planetary shield/Legends|planetary shield]], the [[Ground warfare/Legends|fighting moved]] to the surface, but Admiral Trynn ultimately ordered the [[Orbital bombardment/Legends|orbital bombarment]] of the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Harazod]], two [[Standard day/Legends|days]] after arrival in the [[Gerrard system/Legends|system]]. The incident was reported on by [[Imperial HoloVision]].<ref name="Galaxy Wide NewsNets">{{JournalCite|3|Galaxywide NewsNets}}</ref>

[[Jak Durasha]] of the Imperial Navy was stationed aboard the ''Relentless''<ref name="A Certain Point of View">{{JournalCite|8|A Certain Point of View (short story)|reprint=1}}</ref> in the year [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]].<ref name="Reader's Companion" /> The ship was, at one point, part of a special [[Aris Sector task force|task force]] in the [[Albarrio sector/Legends|Albarrio sector]], serving [[Moff/Legends|Moff]] [[Vanko]]. Adjacent to the [[Sector/Legends|sector]] was the [[Maelstrom Nebula/Legends|Maelstrom Nebula]], home of [[Pirate/Legends|pirates]] who were preying on Imperial shipping in the region. The [[Task force/Legends|task force]] was unable to protect the Moff from the pirates, however, as he was secretly aboard the [[Luxury liner/Legends|luxury liner]] ''[[Kuari Princess/Legends|Kuari Princess]]'' for a covert meeting when the ship was [[Attack on the Kuari Princess|attacked]] by the pirate group known as the [[Riders of the Maelstrom]].<ref name="Maelstrom" />

Around the [[Time/Legends|time]] that the Empire [[Yavin blockade|blockaded]] [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]]<ref name="Fact File 58">{{FactFile|58|YAV 11-12|The Battle of Yavin – Vader's Escape}}</ref> in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]],<ref name="The Essential Chronology">''[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|The Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the ''Relentless'' [[Battle in the Dalchon system|captured]] three pirate [[Starship/Legends|vessels]] while patrolling the [[Dalchon system/Legends|Dalchon system]]. During the [[Space warfare/Legends|engagement]], the Star Destroyer suffered heavy damage to its [[Hyperdrive/Legends|hyperdrive]] [[Engine/Legends|engines]]. The ''Relentless''{{'s}} [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Ranif Parlan]] interrogated the [[Prisoner/Legends|prisoners]] as his ship docked at [[Kwenn Space Station/Legends|Kwenn Space Station]] to undergo repairs, and the pirate [[Quist (pirate)|Quist]] offered  information in exchange for his life: the location of Imperial fugitive [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon]]. Parlan hired the [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] [[Jodo Kast]] to capture Tallon on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], and he additionally sent out a [[Tatoo system/Legends|system]]-wide [[Imperial Bounty 82,471|reward notice]] for the wanted man.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" />

Undercover [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] [[operative]] [[Dana (Rebel Alliance)|Dana]], who had been promoted to Parlan's assistant aboard the ''Relentless'' after three [[Standard month/Legends|months]] behind enemy lines, was present at the interrogation. She felt that Tallon would be valuable to the Rebel cause, and she [[Code Green|contacted]] Rebel [[Agent/Legends|agents]] with instructions to meet her at [[Kwenn/Legends|Kwenn]] [[Space station/Legends|Space Station]]. Her duplicity was discovered, however, and she was [[Death/Legends|killed]]; the Rebels were able to recover her [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]] after a [[Lightfight|fight]] with the ''Relentless''{{'s}} [[Lieutenant/Legends|Lieutenant]] [[Voor (lieutenant)|Voor]]. Afterward, the ''Relentless''{{'s}} security was tripled, and Imperial [[Trooper/Legends|troopers]] sealed the station for twenty-four [[Standard hour/Legends|hours]]. Ship-to-ship searches for Voor's attackers were conducted.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" />

[[File:Escape from Tatooine.jpg|thumb|right|275px|The ''Relentless'' chases the ''Alabak's Gold'' above Tatooine.]]
The ''Relentless'' took on supplies and had its [[hyperdrive activator]]s overhauled, and repairs continued for three days while the Rebels and bounty hunters [[Escape from Tatooine|duked it out]] on Tatooine. Finally, the ''Relentless'' was able to go to [[Lightspeed/Legends|lightspeed]] and head for Tatooine itself; en route, Captain Parlan contacted the Empire's [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] via [[Hologram/Legends|hologram]] and informed him of their progress. Upon the destroyer's reversion to [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]], it found the Rebels escaping the desert world with Tallon aboard the [[Wander-class jump freighter|freighter]] ''[[Alabak's Gold]]''.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" />

Tallon's modified [[Z-95-AF4 Headhunter/Legends|Z-95 Headhunters]] helped the Rebels [[Starfighter combat/Legends|stave off]] [[TIE/IN interceptor/Legends|TIE interceptors]], and they escaped into [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]]. Displeased with Parlan's failure, [[Lord/Legends|Lord]] Vader [[Telekinesis/Legends|choked]] his life away when the captain made his report to Vader's hologram.<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" /> Parlan was replaced as skipper by Captain [[Westen]],<ref name="CSWE Parlan">{{CSWECite|III|13|Parlan}}</ref> who presided over the ship during the [[battle of Heterkus]].<ref name="Rules Companion" />

===Losing ground===
{{Quote|Sir? That's the ''Relentless'' out there. She's an Imperial-class ship. Going in alone seems&hellip;''"<br />"''&hellip;foolish. Thank you, lieutenant. Normally you would be correct, if I did not know something of her commander and crew. G'hengle, would you be so kind as to open up an Imperial channel. With Parlan gone, I will be fighting Westen. I would like him to know who he is facing&hellip;|The [[Unidentified Rebel lieutenant (Silent Water)|pilot]] of the ''Silent Water'' and its captain, Adar Tallon|<ref name="Rules Companion" />}}
The ''Relentless'' was the lead ship of three Star Destroyers sent to [[Heterkus]] to bombard the world from [[Orbit/Legends|orbit]], but an [[Alliance Fleet/Legends|Alliance fleet]] arrived while they were obliterating both Rebel strongholds and cities suspected of providing the Rebellion with support. The Empire's [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] engaged the Alliance's [[X-wing starfighter/Legends|X-wing]] and [[RZ-1 A-wing interceptor/Legends|A-wing starfighters]], while the Star Destroyers began firing their long-range [[Turbolaser/Legends|turbolasers]]. The Rebel [[Flagship/Legends|flagship]] ''[[Silent Water]]''&mdash;commanded by Adar Tallon&mdash;accelerated toward the ''Relentless'', and Tallon's [[G'hengle|comm officer]] opened a [[Comm unit/Legends|communications]] channel to Westen.<ref name="Rules Companion" />

Before the Rebel Alliance's [[Evacuation of Yavin]]<ref name="Rieekan New Fact File">{{FactFile2014|10|RIE 1-2|General Rieekan}}</ref> in 0 ABY,<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> the ''Relentless'', ''[[Avenger/Legends|Avenger]]'', and ''[[Devastator/Legends|Devastator]]'' were ordered to rendezvous at the planet [[Dankayo/Legends|Dankayo]] and [[Battle of Dankayo|reduce]] a [[Dankayo Base|Rebel base]] to slag. The base was the hub of [[Alliance Intelligence/Legends|Alliance Intelligence]] within three sectors, however, and it intercepted the message containing the Star Destroyer's orders. Following the bombardment, not a single being&mdash;living or dead&mdash;was discovered on the planet. The [[Imperial Armored Transport|Imperial transport]] ''[[Elusive (transport)|Elusive]]'' remained behind while the rest of the task force departed the [[Dankayo system/Legends|system]].<ref name="Scavenger Hunt">[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|''Scavenger Hunt'']]</ref>

[[File:Relentlessvslongshot.jpg|thumb|left|250px|The ''Relentless'' sends TIE fighters after the ''Long Shot''.]]
At some point between 0 ABY<ref name="Otherspace date note 1">In ''[[Otherspace (adventure)|Otherspace]]'', [[Westen]] is [[Captain/Legends|captain]] of the ''Relentless''. ''[[The Star Wars Rules Companion]]'' names Westen as Captain [[Ranif Parlan]]'s replacement; Parlan is still the [[Imperial-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer's]] skipper in ''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]'', which features [[Adar Tallon/Legends|Adar Tallon's]] [[Escape from Tatooine]]. That escape is stated to happen concurrently with the [[Yavin blockade]] in {{FactFile|58|YAV 11-12|The Battle of Yavin – Vader's Escape}}, and ''[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|The Essential Chronology]]'' dates the [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin]] [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] to [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> and [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]],<ref name="Otherspace date note 2">''[[Alliance Intelligence Reports]]'' is set two years after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] and mentions the events of ''[[Otherspace II: Invasion]]''.</ref> the Rebel [[Prison ship/Legends|prison ship]] ''[[Celestial (starship)|Celestial]]'' was [[Mutiny on the Celestial|commandeered]] by an escaped prisoner, Imperial [[Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Bane Nothos]], and a [[Distress beacon/Legends|distress signal]] was sent to the nearest Imperial base. The ''Relentless'' responded, but upon arrival at the ''Celestial''{{'s}} location, it found the prison ship gone&mdash;its captain, [[Alain Gryphon]], had desperately sent it to lightspeed despite a damaged hyperdrive. The ''Relentless'' launched a [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of TIE [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]], which engaged the Rebel [[GX1 short hauler/Legends|ship]] ''[[Long Shot]]'' when it appeared on the scene. The newcomers collided with one of the TIEs, giving them a damaged hyperdrive as well.<ref name="Otherspace">[[Otherspace (adventure)|''Otherspace'']]</ref>

The ''Relentless''{{'s}} crew calculated possible locations to which the ''Celestial'' could have jumped, but one of Westen's [[Unidentified Imperial lieutenant (Westen)|lieutenants]] informed him that none of them stood out over the others. Westen&mdash;mindful of his predecessor's fate after disappointing Lord Vader&mdash;opted to wait and see if the newly-arrived Rebels had more information before he acted, and he told his nervous lieutenant that any blame for their failure would be shared. Westen's gambit failed when his target escaped into hyperspace, and the damaged hyperdrives of both the ''Celestial'' and the ''Long Shot'' sent them into a mysterious dimension known as "[[Otherspace]]."<ref name="Otherspace" /> Vader relieved Westen of his captaincy following the man's failure.<ref name="CSWE Relentless">{{CSWECite|III|91|Relentless}}</ref>

Captain [[Dorja]] assumed command of the ''Relentless'' before the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> of [[4 ABY/Legends|4 ABY]].<ref name="NEC" /> His was a cautious command style, and he was reluctant to engage enemies in direct combat.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> The [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]] between the Empire and the Rebel Alliance reached a major turning point at [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], where the Empire's massive [[Death Star II/Legends|Death Star II]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]] was under construction in the space above the [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. Hoping to finish the Alliance off, [[Galactic Emperor/Legends|Emperor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] drew the Rebels into a trap.<ref name="Return of the Jedi">{{Film|VI}}</ref>

[[File:Relentless2-Otherspace.jpg|thumb|right|250px|The ''Long Shot'' escapes from the ''Relentless''.]]
When the Alliance [[Fleet/Legends|Fleet]] arrived in the [[Endor system/Legends|system]] to destroy the incomplete [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]], waiting for them on the far side of the moon<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> was [[Death Squadron/Legends|Death Squadron]]&mdash;thirty-three Imperial Star Destroyers, the [[Executor-class Star Dreadnought/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] ''[[Executor/Legends|Executor]]'', and various other ships.<ref name="Warfare" /> The ''Relentless'' was part of the task force, but due to Dorja's command style, it was removed from the main battle lines<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> when the Empire sprung their trap. [[Immobilizer 418 Interdictor-class Heavy Cruiser|Interdictor cruisers]] were also deployed to keep the Rebels from escaping into hyperspace.<ref name="Warfare" />

The tide of the battle turned in the Alliance's favor when a [[Endor strike team/Legends|strike team]] on the [[Tree/Legends|forest]] moon blew up the [[Endor shield generator bunker|shield generator]] that was protecting the Death Star. Rebel [[Snubfighter/Legends|fighters]] entered the station and destroyed it; among its casualties were [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader and the [[Emperor/Legends|Emperor]].<ref name="Return of the Jedi" /> Death Squadron fought on for nearly four more hours, but the loss of the Death Star impacted the Empire's forces severely: ship-to-ship communications were almost completely disrupted, as were Imperial scanning systems and [[HoloNet/Legends|contact]] with the outside [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="TAB Sourcebook">''[[The Truce at Bakura Sourcebook]]''</ref>

Morale became extremely low<ref name="TAB Sourcebook" /> as Imperial losses mounted: the ''Executor'', the [[Battlecruiser/Legends|battlecruiser]] [[Pride of Tarlandia/Legends|''Pride of Tarlandia'']], and sixteen additional Star Destroyers were all taken out.<ref name="Warfare" /> Caught unprepared for the massive reduction in communications, the Imperial ships' unified [[Blockade/Legends|blockade]] had degenerated into a series of fierce single engagements.<ref name="TAB Sourcebook" /> Command of Death Squadron fell to the Star Destroyer ''[[Chimaera/Legends|Chimaera]]'', whose captain, [[Gilad Pellaeon/Legends|Gilad Pellaeon]], saw his forces in disarray and ordered a retreat to [[Annaj/Legends|Annaj]].<ref name="Warfare" /> Dorja almost refused to follow Pellaeon, an [[Imperial officer/Legends|officer]] [[Junior officer/Legends|junior]] to himself, but he agreed with the man's assessment of the situation and his orders to flee. The ''Relentless'' suffered no casualties during the battle.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" />

===A new hope===
{{Quote|Looks like our old friends are back. They seem to have recovered from that scare we gave them at Linuri. A nuisance, especially right now."''<br />''"Unfortunately, indications are that they're about to become more than just a nuisance. One of the two ships they were rescuing was identified by the ''Relentless'' as the ''Lady Luck''. With Han Solo and Lando Calrissian aboard.|Captain Pellaeon and Grand Admiral Thrawn|<ref name="DFR" />}}
Following a two-day journey to Annaj, Pellaeon chaired a council of war and advocated for a return to Endor with their still-formidable armada. Command was ceded to [[Adye Prittick]], the ranking admiral, but his indecision set off bitter arguing between the present [[Flag officer/Legends|flag officers]]. Admiral [[Blitzer Harrsk]] took a sizeable slice of the fleet into the [[Deep Core/Legends|Deep Core]] until a clear chain of command could be established, and Death Squadron suddenly found itself too depleted to guarantee a victory. Prittick thus ordered a retreat to [[Yag'Dhul/Legends|Yag'Dhul]], while all over the Empire, more and more officers broke off to become [[Warlord/Legends|warlords]] or fortify their own holdings.<ref name="Warfare" />

[[File:Raid on New Cov.jpg|thumb|left|350px|The ''Relentless'' chases the ''Lady Luck'' at New Cov.]]
Command of the fleet fell back to Pellaeon,<ref name="NEGTC">''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]''</ref>, and Dorja followed him throughout the proceeding years. He intended, however, to wrest power from the man.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> When [[Ysanne Isard]], the [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]], assumed the Imperial throne,<ref name="NEC" /> Pellaeon brought the surviving fleet back to the Imperial [[Capital/Legends|capital]] of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. It served under Isard for several years until she [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|lost]] Coruscant to the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Pellaeon nevertheless continued to hold the seemingly-doomed fleet together in the face of both Imperial warlordism and New Republic aggression,<ref name="NEGTC" /> but several times, Dorja came very close to seizing command of the Empire for himself.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" />

Although the Empire's days seemed numbered,<ref name="Warfare" /> Dorja was about to make his move<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> when a visionary leader&mdash;[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn]]&mdash;suddenly returned from the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]<ref name="Warfare" /> in [[8 ABY/Legends|8 ABY]],<ref name="A Grand Admiral Returns">{{WEGCite|story=A Grand Admiral Returns|book=Heir to the Empire Sourcebook|reprint=1}}</ref> marking an end to Dorja's plotting.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> Thrawn rallied the remaining Moffs under his banner and was given nominal control of the [[Imperial Military/Legends|Imperial Military]] by the [[Imperial Ruling Council/Legends|Ruling Council]]. Two isolationist warlord fiefdoms also pledged him their forces: the [[Pentastar Alignment]] and the [[Ciutric Hegemony]].<ref name="Warfare" />

Thrawn was forced to use some of his [[Thrawn's confederation|confederation's]] fleet to protect the Moffs and to defend the Imperial capital of [[Orinda/Legends|Orinda]], while he was given [[Thrawn's fleet (Galactic Empire)|command]] of the twelve remaining Star Destroyers of Death Squadron. Six of those ships were deemed fully loyal, and the ''Relentless'' was not among them&mdash;instead, Dorja and the ''Relentless'' led a secondary force of the remaining six.<ref name="Warfare" /> Dorja interpreted this exclusion as a personal slight, and he balked at the idea of Thrawn, a [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]], being in charge of the Empire. He kept his head low, however, waiting for the day when he could personally restore the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]] to its former glory.<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" />

Thrawn reorganized the Imperial fleet and executed strategic raids along the Empire's border with the New Republic for six months, deeply impressing the Moffs and other [[Politics/Legends|political]] leaders. He was effectively handed the reigns of the Empire, and he stepped up his [[Thrawn campaign|campaign]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]], at a time when [[Imperial Space]] had been reduced to a quarter of its former size.<ref name="NEC" /> When the ''Relentless'' was sent on a [[Raid on New Cov|raid of New Cov]] for a regular collection of taxes on the refined [[biomolecule]]s that the [[New Cov/Legends|planet]] exported, it came across some high-profile targets: former New Republic [[General/Legends|General]] [[Lando Calrissian/Legends|Lando Calrissian's]] [[Personal Luxury Yacht 3000/Legends|yacht]], the [[Lady Luck/Legends|''Lady Luck'']], and the [[AA-589/Legends|personal X-wing]] of the [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].<ref name="DFR" />

[[File:Escapetherelentless.jpg|thumb|right|350px|Luke Skywalker escapes from the ''Relentless''.]]
The ''Relentless'' sent three [[Dropship/Legends|dropships]] full of [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]] and [[Imperial Army trooper/Legends|army troopers]] to the city of [[Ilic]] to search for the enemies of the Empire, but the quarry managed to escape New Cov in their ships. The ''Relentless'' gave chase through the [[Churba system|system]], also sending TIE fighters after their targets, but three ancient [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|dreadnaughts]] suddenly decanted from hyperspace. Belonging to the New Republic's would-be ally, former [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Old Republic]] [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]], the [[Dreadnaught/Legends|dreadnaughts]] began pelting the larger ''Relentless'' with their [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion cannons]].<ref name="DFR" />

The damage done to the Star Destroyer's systems allowed the X-wing, the yacht, and the dreadnaughts to all escape into hyperspace, but the ''Relentless'' managed to take one prisoner: the ship [[Thief/Legends|thief]] [[Niles Ferrier]], who had been attempting to [[Smuggler/Legends|smuggle]] biomolecules off of New Cov. Two days later, Thrawn and Pellaeon watched the ''Relentless''{{'s}} footage of its skirmish with the dreadnaughts, and the Grand Admiral contacted Captain Dorja and his captive via hologram.<ref name="DFR" />

Thrawn told Ferrier to track down the source of the dreadnaughts in exchange for clemency, and he instructed Dorja to provide the thief with a [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] equipped with a three-month [[Self-destruct mechanism/Legends|doomsday clock]]. Meanwhile, Ferrier's own ship would remain aboard the ''Relentless''. The dreadnaughts had in fact come from the legendary lost [[Katana fleet|''Katana'' fleet]], and Ferrier was able to help Thrawn [[Raid on Pantolomin|find]] the [[Hoffner|man]] who had sold them to Bel Iblis.<ref name="DFR" />

===On the ropes===
The lost armada's secret location was revealed to Thrawn,<ref name="DFR" /> and he [[Battle for the Katana fleet|made off]] with 178 of the fabled vessels. With so many [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ships]] now in his hands, he changed tactics and began to openly reclaim territory for the Empire.<ref name="Warfare" /> The Grand Admiral took the ''Chimaera'' to [[Battle at Ukio|capture]] [[Ukio/Legends|Ukio]] while his other Star Destroyers, including the ''Relentless'', were dispatched to make feints elsewhere in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], their goal being to draw the [[New Republic Defense Fleet/Legends|New Republic Defense Fleet]] away from the real strike. Dorja was contacted by Thrawn prior to his feint and given an all-clear to go.<ref name="The Last Command">''[[The Last Command]]''</ref>

[[File:Relentless-classicadventuresvolumethree.jpg|thumb|left|225px|The ''Relentless'' approaches.]]
Not long afterward, while the ''Chimaera'' was at the [[Bilbringi Shipyards]], Pellaeon contacted Dorja and commissioned the six-hour use of a 500-man caretaker crew from the ''Relentless''. The request came after the insane [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Joruus C'baoth]], whom Thrawn had recruited as part of his campaign, used [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] to briefly take control of the ''Chimaera''{{'s}} entire complement, leaving the crew limp and exhausted. C'baoth was later [[Assault on Mount Tantiss|killed]] in his [[Mount Tantiss/Legends|retreat]] on the planet [[Wayland/Legends|Wayland]], concurrently with a [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|battle]] at [[Bilbringi system/Legends|Bilbringi]] that saw the death of Grand Admiral Thrawn.<ref name="The Last Command" />

Thrawn was [[Assassin/Legends|murdered]] by [[Rukh/Legends|Rukh]], his [[Noghri/Legends|Noghri]] [[Bodyguard/Legends|bodyguard]], following revelations that the Grand Admiral had betrayed the Noghri people. Pellaeon ordered a retreat and brought the fleet to a location near the Unknown Regions to assess the situation; although Thrawn had captured enough territory to nearly double the size of Imperial Space, his union splintered in the absence of  his authority. The Empire once again reverted to warlordism, and the New Republic began to recapture its lost territory.<ref name="NEC" /> A devastated Pellaeon brought the ''Chimaera'' into the Unknown Regions, intending to lead all of Thrawn's fleet in a glorious last stand at the edge of civilized space.<ref name="The Last Command Sourcebook">''[[The Last Command Sourcebook]]''</ref>

A group of Moffs and [[Fleet Commander/Legends|Fleet Commanders]] took control of the Empire after Thrawn's death, and the following two years saw an [[Imperial Civil War]], a [[Dark Empire]] [[Operation Shadow Hand|led by]] a reborn Palpatine, and the [[Battle of Ord Cantrell|final death]] of the Empire's [[Crimson Empire|last vestiges]].<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Pellaeon was able to [[Imperial Reunification|unite]] various [[United Warlord Fleets|Deep Core warlords]] and Imperial Rim factions into an [[Imperial Remnant/Legends|Imperial Remnant]] in [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]], however,<ref name="Atlas" /> and [[19 ABY/Legends|seven years later]],<ref name="NEC" /> Dorja and the ''Relentless'' were an active part of the Remnant's navy.<ref name="SotP" />

A shadow of the Empire's former glory, the Remnant held just eight sectors,<ref name="SotP" /> all of which fell within former Pentastar Alignment territory in the Outer Rim.<ref name="Atlas" /> The ''Relentless'' was part of the [[Braxant Sector Fleet]], led by Moff [[Vilim Disra]] from the Remnant's [[Fortress world/Legends|fortress world]] of [[Bastion/Legends|Bastion]],<ref name="SotP" /> but it was also one of the primary vessels used by [[Supreme Commander (Galactic Empire)/Legends|Supreme Commander]] Pellaeon to patrol the Imperial Remnant.<ref name="CSWE Relentless" /> Dorja's attitude toward Pellaeon had softened over the past decade, and he trusted his Supreme Commander's word and judgment.<ref name="VotF" />

When Pellaeon decided that a peace treaty with the New Republic was the only way to guarantee the Remnant's future, an incredulous Disra began to plot against him. He summoned four of his thirteen Star Destroyer captains, including Dorja, to his [[Disra's palace|palace]] on Bastion with new orders for them, but all four officers openly questioned his decision to withdraw them from the [[Braxant sector/Legends|sector]] and leave it vulnerable to attack. Dorja pointed out that Disra lacked the authority to order them into operations outside of the Braxant sector. The four men changed their tune when, to their shock, Grand Admiral Thrawn entered the room and assured them of their missions' importance.<ref name="SotP" />

Dorja, who fondly remembered Thrawn's leadership, eagerly accepted a [[mission to Morishim]] to intercept an [[CR90 corvette/Legends|Imperial courier]]. What he didn't know was that the Grand Admiral was an impostor named [[Flim (Human)|Flim]], who had formed a [[Sinister Triumvirate]] with Disra and [[Major/Legends|Major]] [[Grodin Tierce]]. The [[Courier/Legends|courier]] at [[Morishim]] was Pellaeon's peace entreaty to the New Republic, and the ''Relentless'' dropped out of hyperspace in the [[Morishim system/Legends|Morishim system]] right behind it.<ref name="SotP" />

This corvette carried [[Colonel/Legends|Colonel]] [[Meizh Vermel]], a courier sent by Pellaeon to enter peace negotiations with the New Republic. Later that year, the ''Relentless'' was at the [[Battle of Yaga Minor (Galactic Civil War)|Battle of Yaga Minor]], carrying the triumvirate.

The Galactic Civil War came to an end aboard the [[Bridge (starship)/Legends|bridge]] of the ''Relentless'', where Admiral Pellaeon exposed Flim as a charlatan and the Triumvirate's scheme to seize power came crashing down around them. Before he was arrested, a relieved and cooperative Flim ordered all Imperial forces at [[Yaga Minor/Legends|Yaga Minor]] to cease fire, which allowed Pellaeon and the New Republic to sign [[Pellaeon–Gavrisom Treaty|peace accords]].<ref name="VotF" />

===Yuuzhan Vong War===
[[File:Relentlesstatooinemanhunt2.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The ''Relentless'']]
In [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]], following the Imperial Starfleet's retreat from the [[Battle of Bastion]] and the withdrawal at Yaga Minor, the ''Relentless'' led [[Fleet Group Relentless|Fleet Group ''Relentless'']], one of four temporary battlegroups created for the [[Battle of Borosk (Yuuzhan Vong War)|defense of Borosk]] against the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] invaders. Following the battle, the ''Relentless'' was among the Star Destroyers ordered deployed from Borosk to assist in the [[Battle of Yaga Minor (Yuuzhan Vong War)|defense of Yaga Minor]]. Following Yaga Minor, the ''Relentless'' accompanied the ''[[Right to Rule]]'' on its hunt of the remaining forces of [[B'shith Vorrik]] to [[Generis/Legends|Generis]] and then [[Esfandia/Legends|Esfandia]] where it participated in the [[Battle of Esfandia]].

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|And then, in early July, I got a box from West End Games. It seemed that Lucasfilm had decided I ought to coordinate with their ''Star Wars'' role-playing game background stuff. Stuff which, not being a gamer, I'd never heard of. Once again I set off wandering around the house, this time growling and grumping. Here I was, eleven chapters into the book and suddenly there was more research to be done. Finally, I cooled down and started actually reading through the material. And you know what? The stuff was pretty darn good.|Timothy Zahn|<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook">''[[The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook]]''</ref>}}
The ''Relentless'' first appeared in the ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]'' adventure book ''[[Tatooine Manhunt]]'', published by [[West End Games]] in [[1988]]. The book was written by [[Bill Slavicsek]], [[Daniel Greenberg]], and [[Douglas Kaufman|Doug Kaufman]].<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" /> The ship went on to appear in Slaviscek's next adventure book, ''[[Otherspace (adventure)|Otherspace]]'', as well as the adventure books ''[[Scavenger Hunt (adventure)|Scavenger Hunt]]'' and ''[[Riders of the Maelstrom (adventure)|Riders of the Maelstrom]]''. All three were published in [[1989]].<ref name="Maelstrom" /><ref name="Scavenger Hunt" /><ref name="Otherspace" />

Also in 1989, [[Bantam Spectra]] and [[Lucasfilm]] contacted author [[Timothy Zahn]] about writing a new [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|trilogy]] of ''[[Star Wars]]'' novels, and in [[1990]], they decided that he should coordinate his [[Star Wars Legends|continuity]] with ''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game''. Zahn became enthusiastic about the idea after reading through various material that was sent to him,<ref name="The Thrawn Trilogy Sourcebook" /> and the ''Relentless'' appeared in Books Two and Three of his trilogy: [[1992]]'s ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'' and [[1993]]'s ''[[The Last Command]]''.<ref name="DFR" /><ref name="The Last Command" />

[[File:Attacktherelentless.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The player attacks the "''Relentless''" in the PC game ''Star Wars: X-Wing Tour of Duty: B-Wing''.]]
The Star Destroyer appeared again in the [[Specter of the Past|two]] [[Vision of the Future|books]] of Zahn's followup [[Star Wars: The Hand of Thrawn Duology|''Hand of Thrawn'' Duology]] ([[1997]]&ndash;[[1998]]), which featured the final shots of the Galactic Civil War being fired during a climactic scene aboard the ''Relentless''{{'s}} bridge.<ref name="VotF" /><ref name="SotP" /> It was also mentioned in three issues of West End Games' 1990s ''[[Star Wars Adventure Journal]]''<ref name="Passages" /><ref name="Galaxy Wide NewsNets" /><ref name="A Certain Point of View" /> and featured in several novels of ''[[Star Wars: The New Jedi Order|The New Jedi Order]]'' ([[1999]]&ndash;[[2003]]).<ref name="Ruin">''[[The New Jedi Order: Dark Tide II: Ruin]]''</ref><ref name="Remnant">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic I: Remnant]]''</ref><ref name="Reunion">''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion]]''</ref>

An ''Imperial''-class Star Destroyer called the ''[[Relentless (Sunaj IV)|Relentless]]'' appears in ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Tour of Duty: B-Wing]]'', a 1993 expansion pack of the PC game ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing (video game)|Star Wars: X-Wing]]''. The ship is destroyed by the player character, however<ref name="X-Wing PC Game">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Tour of Duty: B-Wing]]''</ref>&mdash;a destruction that is confirmed by an in-universe "[[Keyan Farlander/Legends|Farlander's]] After-Action Report" in the game's [[X-Wing Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]]<ref name="X-Wing Strategy Guide">''[[X-Wing Collector's CD-ROM: The Official Strategy Guide]]''</ref>&mdash;and as such, [[Wookieepedia]] treats the ship as a different Star Destroyer also named ''Relentless''.

The 1998 video game ''[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|Star Wars: Rebellion]]'' profiles Captain Dorja, stating that he "is in command of an Imperial Star Destroyer" that has not suffered any casualties during the war while under his command.<ref name="Rebellion video game">''[[Star Wars: Rebellion (video game)|Star Wars: Rebellion]]''</ref> Although this description is similar to the ''[[Dark Force Rising Sourcebook]]''{{'s}} profile of Dorja and the ''Relentless'',<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> the game is set in 0 ABY, immediately after the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]],<ref name="Rebellion video game" /> at a time when the ''Relentless'' may not yet have been Dorja's Star Destroyer.

The ''Relentless'' features in several post-Yavin<ref name="Fact File 58" /><ref name="Rieekan New Fact File" /> adventures under the command of Dorja's predecessors, Captains Parlan and Westen,<ref name="Tatooine Manhunt" /><ref name="Rules Companion" /><ref name="Scavenger Hunt" /> and Westen's final mission as skipper is during the events of ''Otherspace'',<ref name="Otherspace" /> known only to be set at some point between 0 ABY<ref name="Otherspace date note 1" /> and 2 ABY.<ref name="Otherspace date note 2" /> The earliest given date for Dorja's command of the ''Relentless'' is "before the Battle of Endor"<ref name="Dark Force Rising Sourcebook" /> (4 ABY),<ref name="NEC" /> and as such, this article avoids making the assertion that the Star Destroyer mentioned in ''Star Wars: Rebellion'' is definitely the ''Relentless''.
